scope: 41 document-level proposals from 16 official file-unit PDFs, January 1989–March 1992: 37 for document treatment and four for annotation. The latest 30 emphasize U.S. policy toward international financial institutions, including IMF resources, development-bank voting, EBRD design, and development-finance coordination. This selective set does not claim complete coverage of the administration or any collection.
method: Read the official PDF’s first page for archival provenance, then inspect each selected document and its final page for authorship, date, boundaries, classification, and release evidence. Preserve redactions, draft and uncertain-date status, and distinguish proposed excerpts from complete documents. Editorial proposals remain subject to compiler judgment and comparison of controlling copies.

documents.title: Paris Economic Summit Preparatory Meeting
documents.selectionRationale: Consider for the opening of the Paris summit sequence: records the agenda reaching Scowcroft after the February Sherpa meeting and the NSC assessment of French intentions. Connects monetary coordination, debt, East-West trade, and the environment before the principals set U.S. objectives.
documents.evidenceNotes: The one-page memorandum is at PDF page 24, routed through Timothy E. Deal and stamped “Natl Sec Advisor has seen.” The attached six-page Sherpa report is represented by a withdrawal sheet on page 25; its contents are not reconstructed here.
documents.editorialReview: Compare with any released copy of McCormack’s report. If that fuller account is selected, consider citing this covering assessment in annotation.

documents.subjectArea: Economic Summits and Industrialized-Country Cooperation
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum; Washington is printed in its letterhead.

documents.title: White House Summit Group Meeting on Paris Summit
documents.selectionRationale: Use in annotation to the March 20 Scowcroft memorandum: the marked action copy shows the staff recommendation and an approval check for arranging the White House Summit Group meeting.
documents.evidenceNotes: Use the annotated copy on page 8; page 10 is a parallel copy with a blank approval line. Page 8 bears a “SIGNED” stamp, an approval check, and a handwritten organizational instruction. It has added Confidential stamps alongside printed “Unclassified with Confidential Attachment” markings. The selected copy’s terminal Confidential stamp controls this Source Note.
documents.editorialReview: Do not attribute the handwritten instruction to a particular person without checking the handwriting. Describe the marked copy without printing both copies as separate documents.

documents.title: Paris Economic Summit
documents.selectionRationale: Consider for documenting who set summit strategy: Scowcroft asks his co-chair Sununu to bring Baker and Brady into a White House Summit Group discussion before securing the President’s guidance for the next Sherpa meeting.
documents.evidenceNotes: The dated, initialed copy is on page 3. The undated copy on page 11 is not a second proposal. The selected copy has added Confidential stamps at top and bottom alongside printed “Unclassified with Confidential Attachment” markings; the Source Note reflects the terminal stamp. The Sherpa report remains withdrawn (page 4); agenda, participants, and organization chart follow on pages 5–7.
documents.editorialReview: Retain the dated copy as this proposal’s citation copy; compare the organizational annotation on Melby’s March 15 action memorandum. Initials do not by themselves establish subsequent implementation.

documents.subjectArea: Economic Summits and Industrialized-Country Cooperation
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum; Washington is printed in its letterhead.

documents.title: Economic Policy Directive 1
documents.selectionRationale: Propose for the institutional origins of Bush trade policy. Melby recommends preserving NSC review of the EPC trade strategy because trade with Japan, Europe, and developing countries has national-security implications; he invokes the handling of debt as a precedent.
documents.evidenceNotes: Page 10 is the dated, initialed Melby memorandum, routed through Deal; its approval lines are blank. Page 11 is an undated memorandum prepared for Scowcroft to send to Brady, with a typed name and no visible signature. Brady’s March 21 directive is on pages 12–13. None of these pages should be assigned the date of another document.
documents.editorialReview: Use the Melby action memorandum for the recommendation actually evidenced here. Check whether Scowcroft’s proposed reply was signed or sent before describing it as an executed instruction.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Eric Melby of the National Security Council Staff to the President's Assistant for National Security Affairs (Scowcroft)
documents.subjectArea: Trade Policy and Market Access
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum; Washington is printed in its letterhead.

documents.title: Presidential Briefing on Economic Summit, 2:15 p.m., Monday, June 26, 1989, Cabinet Room
documents.selectionRationale: Use in annotation to identify the staff preparation and routing of Scowcroft’s June 24 presidential briefing. Establishes the planned division of roles between Scowcroft and Sununu.
documents.evidenceNotes: The one-page action memorandum is routed through Deane E. Hoffmann and asks Scowcroft to sign the attached presidential memorandum. It supplies June 21 as the staff-paper date; June 26 is the scheduled meeting date. The attached presidential memorandum appears separately on pages 3–5.
documents.editorialReview: Do not date the presidential briefing June 21 or June 26. Compare handwritten concurrences before attributing drafting or clearance beyond the typed routing.

documents.title: Meeting with the White House Summit Group
documents.selectionRationale: High-priority proposal. A compact statement of U.S. objectives for the Paris summit: stronger monetary coordination, support for the Brady debt strategy, resistance to competing debt proposals, and an ambitious Uruguay Round. It connects exchange-rate policy, commercial-bank negotiations, and presidential bargaining.
documents.evidenceNotes: The initialed three-page briefing is dated June 24; June 26 is the meeting it prepares. Its location in Latin American Files does not limit its substantive coverage to that region. The opening withdrawal inventory lists it, but the three released pages and declassification stamp are present. Page 12 still represents a withheld one-page biography. Agendas and talking points are separate attachments.
documents.editorialReview: Propose the three-page briefing as one document. Route Mexico-specific material by substance while retaining the multilateral debt strategy in Volume XXX; do not mistake the old withdrawal inventory for the present release state.

documents.title: The Economic Summit at Houston
documents.sender: James A. Baker III and Nicholas F. Brady
documents.selectionRationale: Propose alongside Scowcroft’s July 2 assessment. The joint State–Treasury paper sets negotiating objectives and anticipated G-7 positions on agriculture, Soviet and East European assistance, debt, the environment, and China lending. It provides the substantive baseline to which Scowcroft explicitly responds.
documents.evidenceNotes: The eight-page document names both Baker and Brady on page 16. The withdrawal inventory describes Baker alone; the document heading supplies the fuller authorship. The release stamp and all eight document pages are present, ending with Secret on page 23. It is attached to the Houston briefing sequence in the Scowcroft chronological file.
documents.editorialReview: Compare this citation copy with State and Treasury copies before final publication. The fact that it is in Scowcroft’s file does not make him an author or addressee. Coordinate regional passages with the relevant volumes.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Secretary of State Baker and Secretary of the Treasury Brady to President Bush
documents.subjectArea: Economic Summits and Industrialized-Country Cooperation
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum; Washington is printed in its letterhead.

documents.title: Houston Summit: World Bank Lending to China
documents.selectionRationale: Use to annotate the preparation and approximate timing of the undated Scowcroft China-lending memorandum. Lundsager explicitly sends it for the July 2 Kennebunkport briefing and outlines the proposed lending compromise.
documents.evidenceNotes: One-page action memorandum dated July 1, routed through Timothy E. Deal and stamped “Natl Sec Advisor has seen.” It asks for Scowcroft’s signature on the attached memorandum. Neither this request nor the seen stamp establishes presidential approval.
documents.editorialReview: The cover memorandum establishes association with the July 2 briefing, not an exact date or dispatch for its undated attachment. Leave difficult marginalia unattributed.

documents.title: Scope Paper for Houston Summit
documents.selectionRationale: Use in annotation to establish how the NSC scope paper and the Baker–Brady paper were assembled for the President’s Houston briefing book.
documents.evidenceNotes: The dated one-page action memorandum is routed through Deal. It requests signature of the President’s memorandum and identifies the Baker–Brady paper as Tab II. Terminal marking: “Confidential with Secret Attachment”; the eight-page attachment is separately proposed and marked Secret.
documents.editorialReview: Distinguish Melby’s July 1 staff paper from Scowcroft’s July 2 memorandum and Baker–Brady’s June 25 attachment. Do not count the attached papers twice.

documents.title: Houston Summit: World Bank Lending to China
documents.selectionRationale: High-priority proposal for the decision process on China lending. Weighs the weakening G-7 consensus, congressional restrictions, and World Bank plans, then recommends a compromise linking expanded lending to economic reform while preserving U.S. legal constraints.
documents.evidenceNotes: The three-page memorandum is undated and has a typed FROM line. Lundsager’s July 1 covering memorandum (page 5) prepared it for the July 2 briefing. The approval and disapproval lines on page 8 are blank. Page 7 prints “$700 billion,” while the conclusion on page 8 and talking points on page 9 say “$700 million”; preserve and flag this discrepancy in any transcription. The document is released despite its listing on the earlier withdrawal inventory.
documents.editorialReview: Retain an undated dateline and do not claim approval or dispatch. Check the China-volume boundary and any signed or annotated parallel copy before final selection. July 1 is solely the chronology sorting reference supplied by the covering memorandum.
documents.heading: Memorandum From the President's Assistant for National Security Affairs (Scowcroft) to President Bush
documents.dateBasis: Undated document; sorted with the July 1, 1990 covering memorandum. Prepared for a July 2 briefing; that is not an established document date.
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions

documents.title: Houston Economic Summit
documents.selectionRationale: High-priority proposal. Scowcroft links economic leadership to the NATO summit, recommends conditionality for Soviet assistance without a major U.S. cash commitment, and treats agricultural reform in the Uruguay Round as Houston’s central economic opportunity. His discussion connects German unification and COCOM reform with summit bargaining.
documents.evidenceNotes: The dated, initialed memorandum occupies pages 12–14. Its first page refers to the Baker–Brady paper, and the July 1 Melby cover on page 15 identifies the two-paper package. All three pages are released and the terminal marking is Confidential. These recommendations do not by themselves establish the President’s decisions or summit outcomes.
documents.editorialReview: Print as a distinct NSC assessment if space permits, with the Baker–Brady paper as a substantive companion. Compare the President’s briefing-book copy and subsequent summit conversations for annotations and outcome evidence.
documents.heading: Memorandum From the President's Assistant for National Security Affairs (Scowcroft) to President Bush
documents.subjectArea: Economic Summits and Industrialized-Country Cooperation
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum; Washington is printed in its letterhead.

documents.title: U.S. Position at Upcoming G-7 Meeting
documents.selectionRationale: Establishes the administration’s starting position on IMF quotas, international debt guarantees, and G-7 economic surveillance. Contrasts U.S. resistance to additional taxpayer exposure with French and Japanese proposals, and connects institutional reform to the impending debt-strategy review.
documents.evidenceNotes: Three-page action memorandum, initialed by Farrar and stamped as seen by the National Security Adviser. The approval and disapproval lines on PDF page 7 are blank. No classification marking appears on the selected pages.
documents.editorialReview: Use as an opening institutional-policy document. The recommendation to seek a Brady debriefing is a proposal, not evidence that the briefing occurred.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Stephen P. Farrar to Brent Scowcroft
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development: French Initiative
documents.selectionRationale: Explains how France and the EC shaped the new bank before U.S. negotiating positions were settled. Identifies the stakes in membership, democratic conditionality, creditor control, capital shares, and the precedent for admission to other financial institutions.
documents.evidenceNotes: Two-page information memorandum, initialed by Deal, with a seen stamp and declassification notation. Records the January 6 telephone conversation and Key West Sherpa discussions as antecedents.
documents.editorialReview: Select for the origins of U.S. institutional bargaining over the EBRD. Attribute judgments about Attali and European motives to Deal.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Brent Scowcroft
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions

documents.title: EBRD: Brief for the Baker–Brady–Scowcroft Meeting
documents.sender: Timothy E. Deal, Adrian Basora, and Condoleezza Rice
documents.selectionRationale: Sets out NSC recommendations on borrower eligibility, the private-sector mandate, and membership for the EC Commission and European Investment Bank. Shows the proposed diplomatic campaign to change the bank’s design before negotiations.
documents.evidenceNotes: Two-page joint memorandum, routed through Blackwill and Deal, with initials and a seen stamp. The printed sender line spells Rice’s first name “Condoleeza”; the heading uses her standard name. The Mulford attachment begins on PDF page 13 and is outside this item’s extent.
documents.editorialReview: Pair with the separate January 9 conclusions to distinguish proposed positions from the principals’ resulting instructions.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal, Adrian Basora, and Condoleezza Rice to Brent Scowcroft
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: Baker–Brady–Scowcroft Conclusions: China Lending and the EBRD
documents.selectionRationale: Records agreed U.S. instructions on delaying and limiting World Bank loans to China, seeking G-7 coordination, and entering EBRD negotiations with specified conditions. Provides decision evidence across two financial institutions.
documents.evidenceNotes: Two-page memorandum headed “Summary of Conclusions of Meeting with Secretaries Baker and Brady on January 9: China and EBRD.” Initialed by Deal and stamped as seen; the profile on PDF page 8 records “Noted by Scowcroft.”
documents.editorialReview: Treat as Deal’s contemporary summary of conclusions, not a verbatim meeting transcript. Link the basic-human-needs lending policy to the already proposed July 1990 China-lending papers.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Brent Scowcroft
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: EBRD Negotiations: Joint Treasury–State–NSC Assessment
documents.sender: David C. Mulford, Richard T. McCormack, and Timothy E. Deal
documents.recipient: Nicholas F. Brady, James A. Baker III, and Brent Scowcroft
documents.selectionRationale: Gives the negotiating team’s common account of U.S. isolation over the new bank’s size, lending mandate, eligibility, capital denomination, and governance. Particularly useful for the concern that infrastructure lending could displace support for private enterprise.
documents.evidenceNotes: Three-page Treasury memorandum dated January 16, naming all three officials as senders and all three principals as recipients. Filed as the attachment to Deal’s January 22 report. The final page promises a later paper with recommended positions.
documents.editorialReview: Preserve joint authorship and the January 16 document date rather than the January 22 cover date. Pair with Deal’s separate personal assessment, which explicitly supplements this joint memorandum.
documents.heading: Memorandum From David C. Mulford, Richard T. McCormack, and Timothy E. Deal to Nicholas F. Brady, James A. Baker III, and Brent Scowcroft
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: Negotiations for the EBRD: Deal’s Assessment
documents.selectionRationale: Shows the practical limits on U.S. influence in a European-led financial institution. Weighs participation on unwelcome terms against staying out, and assesses differences among prospective borrowers over markets, privatization, and infrastructure finance.
documents.evidenceNotes: Three-page information memorandum with initials and a seen stamp. Its attachment is the separately proposed January 16 joint memorandum on PDF pages 30–32.
documents.editorialReview: Retain as a distinct assessment rather than a duplicate of the attached negotiating report. Attribute its candid descriptions and judgments to Deal.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Brent Scowcroft
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: IEPR Breakfast: EBRD Conditions, Egypt and the IMF, China Loans
documents.sender: Timothy E. Deal and Eric Melby
documents.selectionRationale: Connects U.S. negotiating instructions on the EBRD charter with pressure for IMF flexibility toward Egypt and scheduling of World Bank loans to China. Shows how the same principals managed political conditions and financial discipline across institutions.
documents.evidenceNotes: Three-page memorandum dated January 25 for the January 26 breakfast. Marked “Declassified in Part”; substantial blocks on PDF pages 36 and 37 remain redacted. The visible text supports the institutional proposals summarized here.
documents.editorialReview: Propose the released institutional-policy passages, preserving the redaction notices. Do not reconstruct the withheld text or describe the memorandum as fully released.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal and Eric Melby to Brent Scowcroft
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: EBRD: Conditions for U.S. Participation
documents.selectionRationale: Identifies the conditions that could keep the United States out of the EBRD. Explains why paying capital in a floating ECU raised concerns about open-ended U.S. commitments and precedents for the IMF, World Bank, and regional development banks.
documents.evidenceNotes: Two-page action memorandum. A handwritten mark appears on the approval line on PDF page 48. The attached presidential memorandum on PDF pages 49–52 is a draft revised by State; it is not treated as a signed presidential decision.
documents.editorialReview: Distinguish approval to convey Scowcroft’s concurrence from final presidential approval of U.S. membership. Note that the text expressly withholds attribution to Scowcroft of the Secretaries’ ECU position.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Brent Scowcroft
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: U.S. Membership in the EBRD: Brief for the President’s Brady Meeting
documents.selectionRationale: Presents Scowcroft’s recommendation to join the EBRD despite incomplete success in negotiations. Specifies public/private lending proportions, voting thresholds, borrower categories, and a mechanism to suspend lending after retreat from political or economic reform.
documents.evidenceNotes: Two-page briefing memorandum headed “Meeting with Secretary of the Treasury Nicholas Brady,” dated March 8, with the President-has-seen stamp. The meeting is listed for 1:30–1:50 p.m. in the Oval Office; this is the preparatory brief, not minutes.
documents.editorialReview: Use the recommendation and negotiated package as evidence of U.S. institutional policy. Verify the President’s actual instructions against a separate decision or meeting record; the seen stamp alone does not establish them.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Brent Scowcroft to President Bush
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: EBRD: Lending Rules, Capital, and Governance Negotiations
documents.selectionRationale: Reports agreement on the 40/60 public/private lending split and acceptance of European Investment Bank membership, while capital denomination, U.S. shares, board arrangements, and leadership remained unsettled. Offers a concrete record of how institutional design was negotiated.
documents.evidenceNotes: Two-page information memorandum, initialed by Deal, with Robert Blackwill’s concurrence on the final page. The printed memorandum is addressed to Scowcroft; the seen stamp identifies the Deputy National Security Adviser.
documents.editorialReview: Focus selection on the lending mandate, capital and governance provisions. The discussion of Soviet borrowing is relevant here as a question of bank eligibility and voting rules.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Brent Scowcroft
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: IEPR Breakfast: Arrears, IMF Programs, and Development-Bank Lending
documents.selectionRationale: Shows U.S. choices over clearing Honduran arrears to the IMF, World Bank and IDB; pressing for an IMF mission to Egypt; and conditioning Zambian debt relief on an IMF or World Bank program. Also records remaining EBRD governance questions.
documents.evidenceNotes: Three-page memorandum dated March 28 for the March 29 breakfast, with a seen stamp and staff concurrences. The institutional and country-financing recommendations are visible on PDF pages 13–15.
documents.editorialReview: Prioritize the EBRD and country-financing portions for document treatment. The intervening bilateral U.S.–Soviet trade discussion can be omitted with an editorial indication and routed to the appropriate volume.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Brent Scowcroft
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: International Debt: Commercial Banks and Official Financing
documents.selectionRationale: Explains strains in the Brady strategy across several borrowers and the division of responsibility between commercial creditors and the IMF and World Bank. The Philippines discussion is especially revealing: banks proposed new money while expecting the institutions to finance debt reduction.
documents.evidenceNotes: Two-page memorandum dated July 21, initialed by Deal and stamped as seen. The selected copy carries a handwritten “Good memo” comment. The Negroponte cable is an attachment outside the two-page extent.
documents.editorialReview: Attribute market assessments and predictions to Deal and his unnamed banking contacts. Use the comparative discussion to explain official/private burden sharing, not as proof that predicted moratoria occurred.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Brent Scowcroft
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: Multilateral Assistance to Central America: Designing the Donor Mechanism
documents.sender: David A. Pacelli and Meg Lundsager
documents.selectionRationale: Documents the unresolved design of a proposed G-24 donor mechanism and Treasury’s resistance to an inadequately specified fund. Shows the NSC insisting that State explain how the mechanism would fit the Enterprise for the Americas initiative and existing regional policy.
documents.evidenceNotes: Two-page copy marked “Re-Do,” dated September 11, with both authors named, staff initials, a seen stamp, and a mark on the approval line. The folder title is October 1990; the document date controls its place in the chronology.
documents.editorialReview: Keep the proposed Central American donor group distinct from the G-24 developing-country caucus at the IMF and World Bank. Pair with the October papers on competing funding mechanisms.
documents.heading: Memorandum From David A. Pacelli and Meg Lundsager to Brent Scowcroft
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: OAS Debt Conversion Fund: U.S. Reservations
documents.selectionRationale: Explains U.S. reluctance to endorse a new $500 million OAS debt-conversion fund because of scarce resources, duplication of IDB and AID microenterprise programs, and uncertainty about its relationship to the Enterprise for the Americas. Useful for comparing institutional expansion with use of existing lenders.
documents.evidenceNotes: Two-page memorandum; the second page lists attachments. Initials reading “RG for” appear beside Scowcroft’s typed name, and the copy is stamped “Signed.” The proposed presidential reply is an attachment, not part of this extent.
documents.editorialReview: Identify the signing-for notation in the source note after comparison with the controlling copy. Do not treat a noncommittal acknowledgment as approval of the proposed fund.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Brent Scowcroft to President Bush
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: Enterprise for the Americas: Competing Funds and Coordination Problems
documents.selectionRationale: Provides a candid account of Treasury–State rivalry over development finance. Warns that a separate Central American fund could compete with the EAI investment fund, confuse prospective European and Japanese contributors, and duplicate World Bank consultative arrangements.
documents.evidenceNotes: Four-page action memorandum dated October 12, routed through Pryce and Deal. The copy contains marginal comments and a mark on the approval line. Attachments include the earlier G-24 package, a Tokyo cable, and a Rockefeller letter.
documents.editorialReview: Select chiefly for fund design, donor coordination, and the proposed resolution of overlapping mechanisms. Attribute its favorable assessment of EAI and criticisms of State to Johnson.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Donald C. Johnson to Brent Scowcroft
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: Funding the Partnership for Democracy and Development
documents.sender: Donald C. Johnson and Eric D. Melby
documents.selectionRationale: Shows how the NSC sought to rank competing multilateral funding appeals and reconcile State’s Central American partnership with the President’s EAI. Makes donor commitments, OMB clearance, and U.S. budget constraints central to the design of the new mechanism.
documents.evidenceNotes: Two-page joint action memorandum dated October 29, routed through Pryce and Deal. The final page has an approval mark and handwritten comments; attached cable and State–Treasury memorandum lie outside this item’s extent.
documents.editorialReview: Use as the follow-through to the October 12 warning. The recommendation concerns clearance of proposed language; it does not itself prove that donors supplied additional money.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Donald C. Johnson and Eric D. Melby to Brent Scowcroft
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions

documents.title: World Bank and IDB Lending to Brazil: South America Follow-Up
documents.selectionRationale: Paragraph 2 reports U.S. leadership of a G-7 effort to block World Bank and IDB lending to Brazil pending an agreement with commercial creditors. Paragraph 7 explains the choice of a Partnership for Development and Democracy mechanism over a separate proposed donor group.
documents.evidenceNotes: Two-page memorandum titled “Report on Follow Up Actions to South America Trip,” dated February 8, 1991, with handwritten annotations and “RG for” beside Scowcroft’s name. The first-page archival marker says February 1991, although the Catalog/earlier ledger title says February 1990.
documents.editorialReview: Propose document treatment for paragraphs 2 and 7, marking omissions of regional political matters. Use the PDF’s February 1991 provenance title and document date; do not inherit the Catalog’s erroneous year.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Brent Scowcroft to President Bush
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: Proposed U.S. Contribution to the IMF’s Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility
documents.sender: National Advisory Council on International Monetary and Financial Policies
documents.selectionRationale: Explains the case for a $150 million U.S. contribution to the IMF’s concessional lending facility for poorer countries. Connects U.S. influence, reform conditions, arrears, interest subsidies, and collaboration with the World Bank and IDA, with tables on contributors and costs.
documents.evidenceNotes: Treasury draft circulated for interagency clearance. Title page dated April 1989; ten numbered text pages and five tables follow, ending on PDF page 28. April 7 transmission papers and an April 10 NSC concurrence surround the report. No classification marking appears on the selected report pages.
documents.editorialReview: Compare with the final transmitted or published NAC report before choosing the controlling text. The proposal documents the administration’s case for contributing, not enactment or payment of the appropriation.
documents.heading: Draft Report of the National Advisory Council on International Monetary and Financial Policies to President Bush and Congress
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: April 1989 on the title page. April 7, the Treasury circulation date, is used only as a sorting key; no day is printed on the report.

documents.title: Briefing for the President’s Lunch with World Bank President Conable
documents.selectionRationale: Brings together the World Bank and IMF role in financing Brady-plan debt reduction, the ninth replenishment of IDA, and the political versus technical basis for China lending. Quantifies the gap between Conable’s preferred IDA funding level and likely U.S. congressional support.
documents.evidenceNotes: Two-page presidential briefing dated June 20 for the June 21 luncheon, initialed by Porter. Separate talking-point cards follow on PDF pages 14–15. No classification marking appears on the two briefing pages.
documents.editorialReview: Use the June 20 preparation date rather than the June 21 meeting date. Pair with Deal’s June 21 corrections, especially on the number of China loans and the state of IDA negotiations.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Roger B. Porter to President Bush
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: Conable Meeting: NSC Corrections on Debt, IDA, and China Lending
documents.selectionRationale: Shows the NSC refining the President’s institutional briefing: distinguishing positions among creditor banks, postponing premature IDA negotiations, and correcting the China loan pipeline. It also explains the relationship between IMF membership and entry into the World Bank.
documents.evidenceNotes: Two-page memorandum routed through Deane Hoffmann, initialed by Deal and stamped “APNSA Has Seen.” The selected copy on PDF pages 19–20 repeats the memorandum on pages 10–11; it is counted once.
documents.editorialReview: Retain the corrections as a distinct document, rather than silently rewriting Porter’s briefing. Treat the membership discussion as institutional eligibility policy; bilateral Soviet relations are not the reason for selection.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Brent Scowcroft
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: Baker to Scowcroft: Coordination of U.S. Votes on IFI Loan Requests
documents.selectionRationale: A principal-level request for Scowcroft to redesign consultation before U.S. votes in the financial institutions. Baker accepts economic tests for most loans but argues that Treasury’s short-notice instructions can exclude important foreign-policy considerations.
documents.evidenceNotes: Signed one-page memorandum dated June 22 with a State declassification notation. A duplicate is filed on PDF page 78; the attached State analysis and executive-order extracts are separate documents.
documents.editorialReview: Select as the initiating principal-level intervention and pair with Scowcroft’s July 25 response. Distinguish Baker’s account of the Philippines vote from an independently checked World Bank voting record.
documents.heading: Memorandum From James A. Baker III to Brent Scowcroft
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: Improving the Interagency Loan Review Process
documents.selectionRationale: Supplies concrete alternatives behind the Baker–Scowcroft intervention: minimum notice before negative votes, NSC arbitration, or voting among the principal reviewing agencies. Uses Haiti and Egypt loans to show that the consultation problem extended beyond the Philippines.
documents.evidenceNotes: Two-page State memorandum stamped June 29, 1989. The first page identifies Milam and McAllister; the final-page drafting line gives June 28. No classification marking appears on the memorandum pages.
documents.editorialReview: Use the June 29 memorandum date and preserve the separate drafting date. These are staff proposals, not adopted procedures; compare with Scowcroft’s later signed instruction.
documents.heading: Memorandum From William Milam to Eugene J. McAllister
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: Development-Bank Votes: Deal’s Recommendation to Scowcroft
documents.selectionRationale: Explains where the loan-review machinery failed: Treasury could depart from staff consensus without enough time for State to appeal. Recommends formal notice and an appeal route, anticipates Treasury’s objections, and places the dispute within the National Advisory Council’s responsibilities.
documents.evidenceNotes: Two-page action memorandum, initialed by Deal, with Paal and Rostow concurrences and a handwritten concurrence notation. The memorandum is duplicated on PDF pages 82–83 and counted once. An undated version of the proposed Scowcroft response follows on pages 62–63.
documents.editorialReview: Pair with Baker’s request and Scowcroft’s dated, signed July 25 memorandum. Do not use the undated attachment as a second document selection.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Brent Scowcroft
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: Scowcroft’s Instruction to Review Development-Bank Voting Procedures
documents.recipient: The Secretary of State, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the Acting Director of the International Development Cooperation Agency
documents.selectionRationale: A signed Scowcroft instruction calling for advance notice and an appeals process when U.S. development-bank votes carry foreign-policy consequences. Assigns a review to the international-economics PCC, with unresolved options to go to the President through the Treasury Secretary.
documents.evidenceNotes: Two-page memorandum dated July 25, with Scowcroft’s signature on the second page and staff annotations. It specifies an August 25 target for the review. The undated copy on PDF pages 62–63 is not counted separately.
documents.editorialReview: Distinguish the instruction to develop procedures from evidence that the review was completed. Link to the June 1991 Philippines dispute, where Deal explicitly invokes the resulting appeals mechanism.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Brent Scowcroft to The Secretary of State, the Secretary of the Treasury, and the Acting Director of the International Development Cooperation Agency
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: Scowcroft to Bush: Negotiating an Increase in IMF Quotas
documents.selectionRationale: Reveals the difference between the public U.S. bargaining position on IMF quotas and the increase Bush had authorized negotiators to accept. Places the U.S. position against demands from other Fund members and links the decision to correspondence with Chancellor Kohl.
documents.evidenceNotes: One-page action memorandum dated December 28, 1989, initialed by Scowcroft and stamped “The President Has Seen” and “Signed.” No classification marking appears on this selected memorandum; the signed outgoing January 2 letter follows on PDF page 42.
documents.editorialReview: Keep the December memorandum distinct from the January 2 presidential letter. Compare the final letter and Treasury drafts when annotating the public presentation of the quota decision.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Brent Scowcroft to President Bush
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: Invoking the Appeals Process for a World Bank Loan to the Philippines
documents.recipient: Wilma G. Hall and Dona F. Proctor (for delivery to Scowcroft)
documents.selectionRationale: Shows the 1989 consultation reform being invoked in practice when State and Treasury could not agree on a World Bank environmental loan. Explains why Scowcroft was asked to arbitrate and records the parties’ agreement to that procedure.
documents.evidenceNotes: One-page electronic memorandum dated June 20, 1991, at 16:18 EDT, addressed to Hall and Proctor with an explicit instruction to pass the background to the General. It describes the proposed loan as $220 million; the later Scowcroft paper gives $224 million.
documents.editorialReview: Preserve the actual electronic recipients rather than label this a directly addressed Scowcroft memorandum. Compare the later papers before reconciling the different loan amounts.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Wilma G. Hall and Dona F. Proctor (for delivery to Scowcroft)
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: Scowcroft’s Recommendation on the Philippine Environmental Loan
documents.selectionRationale: Weighs political costs against Treasury’s objections to weak conditions, rapid disbursement, and the precedent for World Bank environmental lending. Records Scowcroft’s recommendation to abstain after mediating between Eagleburger and Robson.
documents.evidenceNotes: Undated one-page memorandum attached to Deal’s dated June 24 action memorandum on PDF page 35. The text reports the June 24 meeting; a handwritten marginal note bears “6-25.” The marginal note’s author is not assigned here.
documents.editorialReview: Keep the document undated, using the June 24 cover only for sorting. Compare the handwritten note and the President’s decision record before attributing final approval. Pair with Baker’s signed memorandum arguing for a yes vote.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Brent Scowcroft to President Bush
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: No date printed on the memorandum. June 24 cover and reported meeting establish the context; June 24 is a sorting key only. A marginal note is dated 6-25.

documents.title: Baker’s Case for a Yes Vote on the Philippine World Bank Loan
documents.selectionRationale: Provides the opposing principal-level recommendation on the same environmental loan. Baker defends its conditions, cites comparable Asian Development Bank and AID operations, and argues that abstention would incur diplomatic costs without stopping the loan.
documents.evidenceNotes: Two-page memorandum dated June 24, signed by Baker. The second page concludes by asking the President to direct a yes vote. No classification marking appears on the selected pages.
documents.editorialReview: Present alongside Scowcroft’s abstention recommendation so the disagreement remains visible. The recommendation does not establish the eventual U.S. vote or the Board’s action.
documents.heading: Memorandum From James A. Baker III to President Bush
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions

documents.title: IMF Quotas: U.S. Share and Congressional Approval
documents.selectionRationale: Explains the agreed quota increase, the U.S. share, and why authorization and appropriation were required even though the quota transaction was not treated as a budget outlay. Connects the administration’s position to the congressional difficulties of the previous increase.
documents.evidenceNotes: One-page information memorandum addressed to Howe, dated March 14, 1992. The copy carries handwritten explanatory notes below the text; their author is not identified. No classification marking appears on the page.
documents.editorialReview: Attribute the numerical and budget-accounting explanation to Deal. Preserve the manuscript comments for editorial comparison, and check implementing legislation before describing the increase as effective.
documents.heading: Memorandum From Timothy E. Deal to Jonathan T. Howe
documents.subjectArea: Monetary Policy, Debt, and International Institutions
documents.dateBasis: Date printed on the selected memorandum.

documents.title: Brady to Scowcroft: Funding International Priorities and the EAI
documents.selectionRationale: Shows how domestic appropriations constrained multilateral commitments. Brady warns that failure to fund the U.S. share of the EAI Multilateral Investment Fund could prevent other countries’ pledged contributions, and asks Scowcroft to review international-affairs priorities.
documents.evidenceNotes: One-page memorandum dated March 17, initialed by Brady. It refers to a prior presidential meeting on EAI and IMF priorities and to the March 31 expiration of the continuing resolution. No classification marking appears on the page.
documents.editorialReview: Use for the relationship between U.S. budget choices and donor commitments. The memorandum reports pledges and funding risks, not completed contributions.
